title: Having and needing
description: Say what you have, what you want, and what you must do.

explanation.summary: Spanish says many feelings and states with tener plus a noun, where English uses a separate verb. I am hungry is tengo hambre. This is the same pattern as the weather, and it comes up all the time.

sections.heading: Tener and the states
sections.body: Tengo hambre is I am hungry. Tengo sed, tengo sueño, tengo miedo, tengo fiebre, tengo ganas de. The noun never takes an article: tengo hambre, not tengo la hambre. And the two nouns that do take one are exceptions you will meet later: tengo una coche is wrong, but tengo el coche is right.

sections.heading: The four verbs you cannot live without
sections.body: Tener is to have. Querer is to want, and its yo form is quiero. Poder is to be able to, and its yo form is puedo. Deber is to owe, and to must: debo ir means I must go. All four have irregular yo forms, and those are the forms you use most.

sections.heading: Hay, and how much there is
sections.body: Hay means there is, and it never changes: hay un banco, hay dos bancos, no hay bancos. To ask how much of something there is, use cuánto: ¿cuánta agua hay? To ask who is there, use quién: ¿quién está aquí?

examples.en: How much money do you have?
